newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS - Prodi hopes 1997 deficit will meet euro terms.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Prodi hopes 1997 deficit will meet euro terms.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday he was counting on Italy meeting deficit conditions in 1997 for membership of Europe's planned single currency after telling a newspaper that the country would miss the target.
Prodi issued a statement on the sensitive issue after an interview in Friday's International Herald Tribune (IHT).

It had quoted him as saying the ratio between the budget deficit and gross domestic product in 1997 would be 3.3 percent, short of the 3.0 percent target laid down by the Maastricht Treaty for entry into Europe's planned monetary union in 1999.

Prodi said in the statement that he had cited 3.3 percent "out of prudence and honesty" because it was the estimate made by the European Commission and because Italy's 1997 budget had not yet been approved by both houses of parliament.
"I stuck to the figures which readers of the newspaper know better," Prodi said.
"Naturally, with approval of the budget by both houses of parliament, the government is counting on meeting the target (of 3.0 percent) contained in the budget itself," Prodi said.
The 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) budget for 1997, one of the toughest in years, is currently making its way through parliament and must be approved by the end of the year.

"In all honesty we will get to 3.3 percent, rather than an exact three percent, meaning we will be in the range," Prodi had told the IHT. "And then we will examine with our European colleagues what we need to do," he said.
He added that in order to meet the Maastricht goal he was prepared "to take extraordinary and supplementary steps if that is deemed necessary."
To avoid having to introduce a supplementary budget in the spring Italy would need a growth rate of two percent in 1997, the IHT quoted Prodi as saying.

The lira was readmitted to the European Union's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) at the weekend in what the government sees as an essential step towards joining European economic and monetary union (EMU) by 1999.
Prodi reaffirmed that he was prepared to resign if Italy failed to join EMU by the planned starting date.

"When I came to government there was no chance of attaining the Maastricht conditions. Now there is a high chance, let us say an increasing chance, and objective observers say there is a better than 50-50 chance of Italy's joining the first wave of countries launching the single currency," he added.
"Failure to make the 1999 EMU target date "would be an enormous tragedy," Prodi said.
